title: Largest Number
statement:
You are given a list of non-negative integers. You may place them in any order and write them one after another (concatenate their decimal representations) to form a single large number.

Print the largest number that can be formed, as a string. The result can be far too large for any integer type, which is why it is printed as text. If every number is `0`, the answer is `0` (never a string of several zeros).

For example, with `2 9 30 31 3 7` the best arrangement is `9 7 3 31 30 2`, which gives `97331302`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated non-negative integers.
outputFormat: Print the largest number that can be formed, as a single string without leading zeros.

examples.explanation: Order the numbers by comparing concatenations. 9 comes first, then 7, then 3 (`331` beats `313`), then 31 (`3130` beats `3031`), then 30, and 2 last because its first digit is smallest. Joining 9, 7, 3, 31, 30, 2 gives `97331302`.
Every arrangement is `000`, which is just the number 0, so print `0`.
The best order is 9, 39, 2, 10: `9`+`39`+`2`+`10` = `939210`. Placing 39 before 9 gives `399...`, which is smaller.

complexity.time: O(n log n · L), where L ≤ 10 is the number of digits

hints: Sorting the numbers in descending numeric order does not work. Try 30 and 3: numeric order gives `303`, but `330` is larger.
Decide which of two numbers `a` and `b` should come first by comparing the two concatenations `a+b` and `b+a` as strings.
That pairwise comparison is consistent (transitive), so you can use it as a custom sort order. Remember the all-zeros case.
